name: EverShop
title: EverShop SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on EverShop: 25 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; reviews, wishlist and vendors are gaps. Setup, env and fixes.
lede: Solid core coverage: cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against EverShop’s API. EverShop is single-store, single-vendor and single-currency, and the recorded gaps are reviews, wishlist and vendors.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews, wishlist and vendors are not.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your EverShop store

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both.

env.name: PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_API_URL
env.note: Your EverShop store’s URL. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: Sent as a bearer token when set.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/evershop-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_CHANNEL_ID`, but EverShop is single-store, single-vendor and single-currency, so the connector leaves them unused; `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_API_KEY`, `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_API_SECRET` and `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_ACCESS_KEY` are not read either.
backendSettings: Let the storefront’s origin make cross-origin requests to EverShop (CORS): in production the browser calls `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_API_URL` directly, not only the server.
howItWorks: EverShop is a single store with one vendor and one currency, so there is no store or channel to choose: the connector talks to the one store at the URL you give it. Its recurring gaps are the ones CONNECTORS.md sees across this group of platforms — wishlist, reviews and coupon lookup — where the authors could not find an endpoint and would rather ask than invent one.

Installing the package is the whole switch. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever `@misiki/*-connector` is installed, and `src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts` hands it every `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_*` variable that is set, camel-cased, at boot — in the server hook for server rendering and in the client hook for the browser, which must reach the same URL in production.

There is no Litekart API behind the storefront here, so store identity — name, logo, currency, menus, plugin toggles, theme colours — comes from `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` merged under the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`. Until you override it, the store is called “Test”. Any Litekart REST path the connector still inherits is answered from that local data, or resolved empty, rather than requested.
limitations: Pages that depend on a service that is not wired render their empty state rather than failing.
Homepage sections other than the live product list come from the active theme’s static content — the standing rule for themes.
The Conversational Shopping assistant is Litekart-only; its widget stays hidden when another connector is active.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the evershop connector is active but PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/evershop-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “PUBLIC_…_API_URL is set, but it configures a different backend than the one this build runs on”
troubleshooting.fix: Another backend’s variable is still set, usually left over from the one you switched from. Remove it, or install that backend’s connector. `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL` is exempt: it only points the dev proxy.

troubleshooting.problem: The store is called “Test”, or shows the wrong name and logo
troubleshooting.fix: Store identity is static on this backend. Set `name`, `logo`, `currencyCode` and the rest in the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`; `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` lists every field.

troubleshooting.problem: `[evershop] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if EverShop has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

troubleshooting.problem: `http proxy error: api/... ECONNREFUSED` in dev
troubleshooting.fix: A Litekart REST path was requested from outside the connector, so its guard never saw it. Vite proxies `/api` to `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL`, or to `localhost:7000`.

`@misiki/kitcommerce-core` declares it as a peer, and `vite.config.ts` redirects that specifier to whichever connector is installed. Make sure exactly one `@misiki/*-connector` is listed in `package.json`.

faq.q: Can I run an EverShop store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews, wishlist and vendors are not. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production EverShop store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to EverShop?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/evershop-connector`, set `PUBLIC_EVERSHOP_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Can EverShop serve several stores or currencies through Svelte Commerce?
faq.a: No. EverShop is single-store, single-vendor and single-currency, so the store and channel variables the guide lists are left unused by the connector.

faq.q: Has the EverShop connector been run against a real EverShop store?
faq.a: Not against a live production instance — no Svelte Commerce connector has been. It was written by reading EverShop’s authoritative API source, and the Svelte Commerce maintainers ask EverShop’s own maintainers for a sandbox to run it against.
